title: Reducing arcs and Yamada-Vogel reducing moves
statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $D$ be an oriented diagram with Seifert picture $S$ (circles plus signed arcs). A **defect region** is a component of $S^2\setminus S$ that contains an **incoherent pair** of Seifert circles both contributing to its boundary, and a **reducing arc** is an arc $\alpha$ in such a region joining an incoherent pair of Seifert circles and meeting $S$ exactly in its endpoints. The **Yamada-Vogel reducing move** (performed along $\alpha$) slides one of the two circles over the other along $\alpha$, a Reidemeister II move of the diagram in which the two circles are replaced in the Seifert picture by two coherent circles joined by two signed arcs of opposite signs. The move and its inverse are allowed diagrams changes; a reducible diagram is one admitting a reducing arc.
strategy: The local picture is the Reidemeister II band slide of the sources; the two new circles are coherent and carry opposite signs, which is the bookkeeping used to prove that the height drops by one. AC enters exactly through the coherence data of the Seifert circles, i.e. through the annulus lemma used to define coherence; the local band slide itself is an explicit Reidemeister II picture.

references.title: Birman and Brendle, Braids: A Survey, Handbook of Knot Theory chapter, author manuscript; section 2 (printed pp. 12-26) and Figures 3-12
Traczyk, A new proof of Markov's braid theorem, Banach Center Publications 42 (1998), 409-419
